expectation: `orderedDestinationGroups` passes the `Map` returned by `groupByDestination` to `orderManifestGroups`, whose comparator reads a `destination` field that the `[key, group]` entries lack, so the groups keep insertion order instead of ascending lexical order.
finding: `groupByDestination` returns a `Map`, and `orderedDestinationGroups` passes that `Map` directly to `orderManifestGroups`, where `[...groups]` yields `[key, records]` tuple arrays whose `.destination` property is `undefined`, so the sort comparator always returns `0` and leaves destination groups in insertion order.

requirementSource.requirement: `orderedDestinationGroups` returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.

expectation: The geocoder contract defines `geocoder.lookup` only for known addresses, so it cannot be established whether an unknown address resolves to `undefined` (left out), resolves to another value (kept) or rejects (the whole call rejects).
finding: `locateStops` assumes `geocoder.lookup(stop.address)` resolves to `undefined` for unknown addresses (`stop.point !== undefined`), while `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md` only specifies `geocoder.lookup(address)` for known addresses and leaves unknown-address behavior unspecified.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md`, `locateStops` leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.

expectation: `withinVehicleCapacity` converts the limit to grams and requires the clamped remainder to be above zero, so a total equal to the limit (remainder 0) is rejected.
finding: `withinVehicleCapacity` checks `remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0`, which evaluates to `0 > 0` (`false`) when `weight` in grams equals `limit * 1000`, rejecting a total equal to the configured vehicle limit.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `withinVehicleCapacity` accepts a total equal to the configured limit.

expectation: `canPlanRoute` checks `routes:admin` in the actor's own scopes instead of its held scopes, so an admin scope held through an active claim does not meet the ownership requirement.
finding: Under Route planning rules 3 and 4 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, held scopes include active claim scopes, but `canPlanRoute` checks `actor.scopes.includes('routes:admin')` instead of `effectiveScopes(actor, now).includes('routes:admin')`, refusing non-owner actors who hold `routes:admin` through an active claim.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` treats an actor holding `routes:admin` as owning every depot.

expectation: `effectiveScopes` drops only the actor's own scopes when it is suspended and still adds active-claim scopes, so a suspended actor with an active `routes:plan` claim can plan.
finding: Under Route planning rule 5 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` (which overrides rule 4), a suspended actor has no held scopes, but `effectiveScopes` still includes scopes from active claims when `actor.suspended === true`, allowing `canPlanRoute` to authorize a suspended actor holding an active `routes:plan` claim.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` refuses every suspended actor.

expectation: `handleAnnouncementFailure` removes the copy returned by `store.get`, and `store.remove` removes only the exact stored object, so the stored manifest is not removed.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `store.get(id)` returns a new copy while `store.remove(manifest)` removes the manifest only when given the exact stored object, so `handleAnnouncementFailure` calling `store.remove(await store.get(manifest.id))` leaves the stored manifest in `store` when `announcer.send` fails.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `publishWithAnnouncement` removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.

expectation: `stripCredentials` recurses only into values whose constructor is `Object`, so credentials inside arrays below `auth` are kept.
finding: `stripCredentials` only traverses values with `value?.constructor === Object`, so credentials (`token`, `secret`, `password`) nested inside arrays or `Object.create(null)` objects below `event.auth` are left unredacted in violation of Credentials rules 23 and 24 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `redactManifestEvent` removes every credential nested below an `auth` field.

expectation: `buildManifest` copies each record shallowly and `labelDriver` assigns the label onto the supplied driver object, so supplied records are mutated.
finding: Although `buildManifest` shallow-copies each outer record (`{...record, ...}`), `labelDriver` calls `Object.assign(driver, {label: preserveManifestDriver(driver.label)})` on `record.driver`, mutating the nested `driver` object of supplied records in place.

requirementSource.requirement: `buildManifest` copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.

expectation: `publishManifest` maps entries through an async callback, and every resulting promise is truthy, so a manifest with invalid entries is stored.
finding: `publishManifest` maps entries with an `async` callback (`manifest.entries.map(async (entry) => manifestEntryIsValid(entry))`), producing `Promise` objects that are always truthy in `checks.every(Boolean)`, so invalid manifest entries pass validation and are stored via `stageManifest`.

requirementSource.requirement: `publishManifest` stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.

expectation: `asPublicationError` marks a failure transient when it has a finite `retryAfter` even if it is marked `transient: false`, so `publishWithRetry` retries a failure rule 27 makes non-transient.
finding: Under Failure classification rule 27 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` (which overrides rule 26), a failure marked `transient: false` is never transient even when it carries a finite numeric `retryAfter`, but `asPublicationError` sets `transient` to `error?.transient === true || Number.isFinite(error?.retryAfter)`, causing `publishWithRetry` to retry `{transient: false, retryAfter: ...}` failures.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `publishWithRetry` retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.

expectation: The public dispatch entry omits the executor surface.
finding: `src/dispatch/index.mjs` re-exports the planning, manifest, publication, and telemetry modules but omits `./executor.mjs`, leaving execution operations (`executeAuthorizedPlan`, `executeDryRun`, `planFailure`, `runEligibleStops`, `emitPlanCreated`, and `pendingStops`) unavailable through the public dispatch entry.

expectation: `coalesceAcrossGroups` records raw package IDs but filters normalized IDs, so a duplicate that differs only in surrounding whitespace survives in a later group.
finding: `coalesceAcrossGroups` normalizes `group.packageIds` before checking `!seen.has(id)` but adds raw unnormalized `group.packageIds` entries to `seen`, so an ID with surrounding whitespace (such as `' P1 '`) in an earlier group does not prevent `'P1'` from appearing again in a later group.

requirementSource.requirement: `coalescePackages` removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.

expectation: `nextRetryDelay` tests `retryAfter` by truthiness, so a server-provided `retryAfter` of 0 falls back to the computed backoff instead of a 0 ms delay.
finding: `nextRetryDelay` checks truthiness (`retryAfter ? ...`) instead of `Number.isFinite(retryAfter)`, so a valid server-provided `retryAfter` of `0` falls back to `computeBackoff(attempt)` instead of `0`, while truthy non-finite or non-numeric values (such as `Infinity` or `"abc"`) replace the computed backoff instead of being ignored under Retry timing rule 7.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `nextRetryDelay` applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided `retryAfter`.

requirementSource.requirement: `executeAuthorizedPlan` rejects an unauthorized caller before invoking dispatch.

expectation: Delivery notices are sent to the raw `phone`, so an entry whose `phone` contains spaces or hyphens is not notified at its contact phone (rule 33).
finding: Under rule 33 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, an entry's contact phone has every space (` `) and hyphen (`-`) removed, but `sendDeliveryNotices` passes raw `entry.phone` directly to `sms.send`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, delivery notices go to the contact phone of every manifest entry.

expectation: Route duration adds the raw `serviceMinutes`, so every stop misses the 5 minutes of parking that rule 32 includes in its service time.
finding: Under rule 32 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop's service time is `serviceMinutes` plus 5 minutes of parking, but `routeDuration` adds only `stop.travelMinutes + stop.serviceMinutes` and omits the 5-minute parking allowance per stop.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.

expectation: A server-provided `retryAfter` of 0 is falsy, so `nextRetryDelay` uses the computed backoff instead of the server delay.
finding: Same as `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md` line 19: `nextRetryDelay` checks truthiness (`retryAfter ? ...`) instead of `Number.isFinite(retryAfter)`, so a server-provided `retryAfter` of `0` falls back to `computeBackoff(attempt)` instead of `0` while truthy non-finite or non-numeric values replace the computed backoff.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next retry delay follows the Retry timing rules whenever the server provides `retryAfter`.

expectation: Manifest-event redaction leaves arrays unvisited, so a credential in an object inside an array of the authentication data is not removed.
finding: Same as `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md` line 23: `stripCredentials` in `redactManifestEvent` only traverses values with `value?.constructor === Object`, leaving credentials (`token`, `secret`, `password`) nested inside arrays or `Object.create(null)` objects below `event.auth` unredacted.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.

expectation: The announcement failure branch passes the new copy from `store.get` to `store.remove`, which removes nothing for any object other than the stored one.
finding: Same as `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md` line 22: under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `store.get(id)` returns a new copy while `store.remove` requires the exact stored `manifest` object, so `handleAnnouncementFailure` removes nothing and fails to roll back the stored manifest when `announcer.send` fails.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.

expectation: Package coalescing compares normalized IDs against raw IDs seen in earlier groups, so whitespace variants of one ID are kept across groups.
finding: Same as `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md` line 48: `coalesceAcrossGroups` checks `!seen.has(id)` on normalized (trimmed) package IDs while adding raw unnormalized `group.packageIds` values to `seen`, leaving duplicate normalized IDs across destination groups when an earlier group contains untrimmed or non-string IDs.

requirementSource.requirement: Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.

expectation: After `renameTemporary` rejects, the temporary bytes are locked, so the `discardTemporary` call in `writePlanAtomically` only closes the write and keeps them; `removeTemporary` is never called.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, temporary bytes are locked after `store.renameTemporary()` rejects, and `store.discardTemporary()` keeps locked bytes instead of deleting them; `writePlanAtomically` calls `store.discardTemporary()` rather than `store.removeTemporary()` in its `catch` block, leaving the temporary bytes behind.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.

expectation: `canAssignAllPackages` delegates to `withinVehicleCapacity`, whose remaining-capacity test is false at zero remainder, so a total equal to the limit is rejected.
finding: `canAssignAllPackages` delegates to `withinVehicleCapacity(totalPackageWeight(packages), limit)`, which checks `remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0` and returns `false` when total package weight in grams equals `limit * 1000`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, assigning all packages accepts a total equal to the vehicle limit.

expectation: The public entry does not export `executor.mjs`.
finding: `src/dispatch/index.mjs` does not export `./executor.mjs`, omitting the execution operations (`executeAuthorizedPlan`, `executeDryRun`, `planFailure`, `runEligibleStops`, `emitPlanCreated`, and `pendingStops`) from the public dispatch entry.

requirementSource.requirement: The public dispatch entry exports the execution operations used by callers.

expectation: Plan serialization sorts only the top-level keys (`withSortedKeys` proxies only the plan object), so nested objects keep their insertion order and plans that differ only in nested field order hash to different values.
finding: `withSortedKeys` only wraps the top-level object in a `Proxy` and does not sort keys on nested objects, so `serializePlan` and `checksumPlan` produce different serialized strings and different plan hashes when two plans differ in field order inside nested objects.

requirementSource.requirement: Two plans that differ only in the order of the fields inside their nested objects have the same plan hash.

expectation: Urgent-stop partitioning tests the raw `priority` for the remaining partition, so a text priority such as `'7'` (priority 5 under rule 15) is placed in no partition.
finding: `partitionUrgentStops` uses `priorityOf(stop) > 5` for `urgent` but `!(stop.priority > 5)` for `remaining`; under Stop priority rules 15 and 16 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop with `priority: Infinity` or a numeric string such as `priority: "10"` has effective priority `5` (not urgent) yet evaluates `stop.priority > 5` as `true`, excluding it from both partitions.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, urgent-stop partitioning places every stop in exactly one partition according to its urgency.

finding: Under rule 32 of `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop's service time is `serviceMinutes` plus 5 minutes of parking, but `routeDuration` adds only `stop.travelMinutes + stop.serviceMinutes` and omits the 5-minute parking allowance per stop.

problemOptions.expectation: Route duration adds the raw `serviceMinutes`, so every stop misses the 5 minutes of parking that rule 32 includes in its service time.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.

finding: Under Departure timing rule 10 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, all departure hours are UTC hours, but `nextDispatchTime` passes local `candidate.getHours()` instead of `candidate.getUTCHours()` to `isWithinBlackout`.

problemOptions.expectation: `nextDispatchTime` checks the blackout with the host-local hour instead of the UTC hour, so on a non-UTC host a time inside the blackout is not moved.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.

finding: Same as `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md` line 28: `emitPlanCreated` passes `() => emitter.emit('plan.created', input.plan.id)` as `onStored` into `savePlan`, which forwards it as `{onCommit: onStored}` to `store.write`, and no contract in the repository defines whether or when `store.write` invokes `onCommit`.

problemOptions.expectation: Plan-created telemetry depends on when the store invokes `onCommit`, which no available contract defines.

requirementSource.requirement: Plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds.

finding: Under Stop priority rule 18 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a stop without a finite numeric `sequence` must follow every stop of equal priority that has one, but `compareStops` only replaces `null` and `undefined` via `?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so stops with non-finite or non-numeric `sequence` values (such as `-Infinity`, `NaN`, `false`, or `""`) do not follow finite numeric sequences (and finite sequences above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` sort after `undefined`).

problemOptions.expectation: The stop comparator coerces a text `sequence` such as `'2'` to a number, so a stop without a finite numeric sequence does not follow the equal-priority stops that have one.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.

finding: `authorizeRouteBatch` returns `firstRejected <= 0` instead of `firstRejected === -1`, so when the first route (`index 0`) fails `requireDepotOwner`, `findIndex` returns `0` and the batch is erroneously authorized.

problemOptions.expectation: `authorizeRouteBatch` accepts the batch when `findIndex` returns 0, so a batch whose first route fails depot ownership is authorized.

requirementSource.requirement: Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.

finding: Under Vehicle capacity rule 28 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, recorded package weights must be in grams, and `weighPackages` records `await scale.read(entry.packageId)` without conversion, while `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md` does not specify the unit returned by `scale.read`.

problemOptions.expectation: The weighing contract does not state the unit of the weight that `scale.read` resolves to, so it cannot be established that weighed package weights are in grams.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, package weighing records each package weight in the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.

finding: Same as `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md` line 20: `executeAuthorizedPlan` awaits `dispatchRoute(dispatch, route)` as a function argument before `unlessForbidden` checks `canPlanRoute(actor, route, now)`, invoking `dispatch(route)` even for unauthorized callers.

problemOptions.expectation: Arguments are evaluated before `unlessForbidden` runs, so authorized execution invokes dispatch before it can reject the caller.

requirementSource.requirement: Authorized execution rejects a caller before invoking dispatch.

finding: `parseRetryCount` converts inputs via `Number(value)` without enforcing whole-number type or base-10 digit text syntax under Retry counts rules 21 and 22 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, accepting invalid values such as `""`, `" 2 "`, `"0x2"`, `"1.0"`, `null`, `false`, `true`, and `[]`.

problemOptions.expectation: Retry-count parsing accepts any text that `Number` converts to an integer from 0 through 3, including text that is not base-10 digits such as `'0x2'`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, retry-count parsing accepts exactly the valid retry counts and rejects every other value.

finding: Under Failure classification rule 27 in `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` (which overrides rule 26), a failure marked `transient: false` is never transient even if it carries a finite numeric `retryAfter`, but `asPublicationError` marks it `transient: true` and `publishWithRetry` retries instead of stopping immediately.

problemOptions.expectation: A failure marked `transient: false` that carries a finite `retryAfter` is rewrapped as transient, so publication retries do not stop for it.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, publication retries stop immediately for failures that the Failure classification rules do not make transient.

problemOptions.expectation: A suspended actor keeps the scopes of its active claims in `effectiveScopes`, so `canPlanRoute` can still allow it.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a suspended actor cannot plan any route.
